doc.title: Toshiko Akiyoshi interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 17, 1999

chapter: Finding her voice as a composer
title: The thirteen difficult years as accumulation
summary: She does not see her thirteen lean years as hardship but as hibernation.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: Day jobs: musicians working outside music

blocks.x: community or history that has been pretty good to me. However people always say that, you know I barely played for about thirteen years, and the people always say well you had a terrible time, a difficult time. And I never thought I am having a difficult time. Because everybody else did I thought. When I look back I think those times were very important times. If I didn’t have that I probably didn’t come to that conclusion. I think it’s having sort of like, not a battle, but to become more warm. It’s very difficult. It’s literally— you know I say there is a certain animal they go sleep in the wintertime.

They go hibernate. But it’s not really a hibernation but there’s a time when you are, and then you accumulate a lot of thought, all the things you accumulate. And that was my thirteen years I think. And that I think was a very important time for me. So I think everything worked the way it should be.
